evidence.title: Kauai Railway
evidence.text: The Kauai Railway is a former narrow gauge railway company in Hawaii, United States.

evidence.title: Kauai Railway
evidence.text: It was created 1906 and operated a 30 km long railroad line with narrow gauge track from Port Allen,to Koloa and Kalaheo on the south coast of the island of Kauai.

evidence.title: Kauai Railway
evidence.text: It did not have a connection to the other common carrier railway on the island, the Ahukini Terminal and Railway, although both were built to the same track gauge.

evidence.title: Kauai Railway
evidence.text: Almost all railway trackage on Kauai was connected together due to an agreement with the U.S. Government to interconnect the common carriers and sugarcane plantation railways.

evidence.title: Kauai Railway
evidence.text: The government imposed this as a condition before they would agree to improve the port of Nawiliwili for oceangoing ships.

evidence.title: Kauai Railway
evidence.text: The line was opened 1907.

evidence.title: Kauai Railway
evidence.text: In 1936 the company name was changed to the Kauai Terminal Company.

evidence.title: Kauai Railway
evidence.text: The last train ran 1947, with rail operations replaced by trucks.

evidence.title: Kauai Railway
evidence.text: The company continues to exist as the present-day Kauai Commercial Company.

evidence.title: Oahu Railway and Land Company
evidence.text: The Oahu Railway and Land Company, or OR&L, was a narrow gauge common carrier railway that served much of the Hawaiian island of Oahu, and was the largest narrow gauge class one common carrier in the U.S, until its dissolution in 1947.

evidence.title: Bodie, California
evidence.text: Bodie ( ) is a ghost town in the Bodie Hills east of the Sierra Nevada mountain range in Mono County, California, United States, about 75 mi southeast of Lake Tahoe.

evidence.title: Bodie, California
evidence.text: It is located 12 mi east-southeast of Bridgeport, at an elevation of 8379 feet (2554 m).

evidence.title: Bodie, California
evidence.text: As Bodie Historic District, the U.S. Department of the Interior recognizes it as a National Historic Landmark.

evidence.title: Lakeside and Marblehead Railroad
evidence.text: Incorporated on April 17, 1886, at Marblehead, Ohio, the Lakeside and Marblehead Railroad (L&M) was a short standard gauge railroad that spanned about seven miles (11.3 km) in length.

evidence.title: Lakeside and Marblehead Railroad
evidence.text: It extended from Marblehead through Lakeside to a connection with the Lake Shore and Michigan Southern Railway (later the New York Central Railroad) at Danbury (an unincorporated hamlet bordering Sandusky Bay).

evidence.title: Lakeside and Marblehead Railroad
evidence.text: A common carrier, it carried both freight and passengers.

evidence.title: Lakeside and Marblehead Railroad
evidence.text: It was abandoned as a common carrier railroad July 31, 1964, operated for the last time as a private industrial railroad in Summer 1978, and its tracks were removed in Fall 1997.

evidence.title: Sandy River Railroad
evidence.text: The Sandy River Railroad was a narrow gauge railway built to serve the towns of Strong and Phillips in the Sandy River valley upstream of Farmington.

evidence.title: Sandy River Railroad
evidence.text: The Sandy River Railroad was the first narrow gauge common carrier railroad built in the State of Maine.

evidence.title: Phillips and Rangeley Railroad
evidence.text: The Phillips and Rangeley Railroad was a narrow gauge common carrier railroad in the State of Maine.

evidence.title: Sandy River and Rangeley Lakes Railroad
evidence.text: The Sandy River & Rangeley Lakes Railroad (SR&RL) was a narrow gauge common carrier railroad that operated approximately 112 mi of track in Franklin County, Maine.

evidence.title: Sandy River and Rangeley Lakes Railroad

evidence.title: Mono Mills Junction, California
evidence.text: Mono Mills Junction (may sometimes be referred to as "Benton Junction") is a location within the Mono Basin in central Mono County where the Mono Mills Road California State Route 120, proceeds eastward from U.S. Route 395.

evidence.title: Mono Mills Junction, California
evidence.text: Route 120 accesses the Mono Lake Tufa State Reserve, including Navy Beach and South Tufa along the shores of Mono Lake, and leads through Mono Mills to Benton where it reaches the U.S. Route 6.

evidence.title: Mono Mills, California
evidence.text: Mono Mills (also, Mono) is a ghost town in Mono County, California.

evidence.title: Mono Mills, California
evidence.text: It is located 9.5 mi east-southeast of Lee Vining, at an elevation of 7356 feet (2242 m).

evidence.title: Mono Mills, California
evidence.text: Mono Mills has nearly vanished.

evidence.title: Mono Mills, California
evidence.text: Its site is along California State Route 120, 9.1 mi east from the junction with U.S. Route 395.
